payload.question_text: Which features can visual embeddings encode? Select all that apply.

Shape is a visual property of image content. Visual embeddings can represent shape-related patterns.
Texture describes a visual surface pattern. Visual embeddings can encode texture with other image features.
Word meaning is represented by language embeddings. It is not itself a visual feature encoded by visual embeddings.
options.better_fit: Word meaning is appropriate when working with a language vocabulary.

evidence.statement: The items accurately cover visual features, paired image-text training, cross-model attention, shared space, contextual visual relationships, and description generation from the source.

A minor source-fidelity risk is that the fill-in item presents “paired image-text data” as a named term, while the source describes images with associated text rather than explicitly naming that term.
Each multiple-choice item has a unique keyed answer set, and the selection instructions distinguish single-choice from select-all-that-apply items.
Arrange and fill-blank items provide explicit correct orders or accepted answers consistent with their prompts.
Distractors such as class labels, bounding boxes, and pixel classes are credible alternatives drawn from adjacent computer-vision tasks without being correct for image-text connection.
The artifact explicitly diagnoses classification, detection, segmentation, modality, training-target, vocabulary, and anthropomorphism confusions.
The sequence moves from recall and reconstruction toward applying concepts in checkout, retailer, and doorbell-camera scenarios.

The ordered session repeats paired-image training at questions 1, 3, and 5, visual embeddings at questions 0, 7, and 10, and language vocabulary only near the end, weakening a clean concept-to-application progression.
The session alternates multiple-choice, arrange-sentence, and fill-blank mechanics across the 14-item sequence.
Prompt stems vary across identification, reconstruction, sequencing, scenario application, and selection tasks, although three arrange-sentence prompts use closely related wording.
Scenarios use credible computer-vision contexts from the source, including smart checkout, grocery retail, and doorbell cameras, and attach them to plausible engineering decisions.
Incorrect-answer feedback identifies the specific misconception and states the governing distinction, such as classification versus image-text pairing or visual patterns versus human understanding.
The artifact mixes remembering, understanding, and applying items, with later scenario questions requiring selection of model components or workflow steps appropriate to a Level 2 session.
Core terms such as visual embeddings, language embeddings, cross-model attention, shared space, and multimodal model are used consistently across the items.
“Paired image-text data” and “language vocabulary” are usable paraphrases, but they are less exact than the source’s “images with associated text descriptions” and “linguistic vocabulary.”
The final sequence is source-aligned, varied in mechanics, and supported by targeted feedback and realistic scenarios.
Repeated near-duplicate recall items and the late introduction of language vocabulary make the session feel more cyclical than progressively integrative.

largest_gap.summary: The session’s concepts are accurate but ordered with repeated recall clusters instead of a clear foundation-to-integration arc.

evidence.statement: Paired-image training is assessed three times before and around the cross-model integration content, while language vocabulary appears only at item 12 of 14; visual embeddings are also revisited three times.

largest_gap.repair_instruction: Reorder the existing items so language vocabulary and visual embeddings are established first, followed by paired image-text training, cross-model attention/shared space, and image-description application; then retain only one or two strategically spaced retrieval items for consolidation. Preserve each item’s keyed answers and identity fields.

result.concise_summary: The artifact is highly source-faithful, unambiguous, varied, and feedback-rich, with no critical deterministic defects. The main remaining issue is session-level progression: repeated concept checks are interleaved and language vocabulary is introduced late. Confidence is reduced because no approved references were supplied.
